summary: Sunday teardown of Geoberry and 60SecondClub for the geography channel: added 1 topic (the world redrawn by its biomes), found that both of Geoforia's breakout Shorts behind two open topics are now removed from YouTube, and skipped five crowded stories.
why: Geoberry gets 62-265x its 3.72K subscribers with whole-world what-ifs. Its only real-world rule that nobody has told this month is the biome map (0 same-story Shorts in 30 days), and it scores 7.71, 5th in the feed. Russia-US swaps, Texas, Hungary's 1920 losses, the most-neighbours story and the Louisiana Purchase each had 5+ new Shorts this week.

findings.title: Geoberry: Every country had to merge with a neighbour, 986K on 3.72K subs (265x)
findings.detail: A one-rule whole-world what-if; its Minecraft biomes Short (231K, 62x) is the reference for tonight's topic.

findings.title: Geoforia's language and empires Shorts are now unavailable
findings.detail: The references for two open topics (421K and 354K) are gone and its Shorts tab is empty. The topics stay, with demand marked removed.

findings.title: 60SecondClub: swaps and collapses got millions (Russia-US 10M) but new ones get 0.4-1.5x its 536K subs
findings.detail: Russia-US swaps are crowded this week (6+ new); its war and collapse what-ifs are outside the profile.

findings.title: The taiga is 17M km², almost Russia's 17.1M km²
findings.detail: The payoff of the biome topic; the Sahara (9.2M km²) would rank fifth among countries.

changes.title: Topic: what if the world's borders followed its forests and deserts?
